statement: Whenever max_score(edges) returns a result r, r is the maximum score over all choices of pairwise non-adjacent edges. Precisely, for distinct i,j with 1 ≤ i,j < n, call edges i and j adjacent iff p_i = p_j or p_i = j or p_j = i; call S ⊆ {1,...,n-1} a matching if no two distinct members of S are adjacent, and let weight(S) = ∑_{i∈S} w_i. Then there exists a matching S with r = weight(S), and for every matching T, weight(T) ≤ r. The empty set is a matching, so this maximum is at least 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). The input satisfies the problem constraints: n ≥ 1 and n ≤ 10^5; every edges[i] has length 2; edges[0][0] = edges[0][1] = -1; for every i with 1 ≤ i < n, setting p_i = edges[i][0] and w_i = edges[i][1], we have 0 ≤ p_i < n, p_i ≠ i, and -10^6 ≤ w_i ≤ 10^6; and the parent map is a tree rooted at 0, i.e. starting from any i ≥ 1 and repeatedly replacing the current node x by p_x while x ≠ 0 eventually reaches 0.

statement: Whenever max_score(edges) returns a result r, r is the maximum weight of a matching all of whose edges have positive weight: there exists a matching S ⊆ {i | 1 ≤ i < n and w_i > 0} with r = ∑_{i∈S} w_i, and for every matching T ⊆ {i | 1 ≤ i < n and w_i > 0}, ∑_{i∈T} w_i ≤ r. Here a matching is a set of indices ≥ 1 no two distinct of which i,j satisfy p_i = p_j or p_i = j or p_j = i.
